title: Use of semaglutide and risk of non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy: a Danish-Norwegian cohort study
authors: Simonsen E, Lund LC, Ernst MT, Hjellvik V, Hegedüs L, Hamann S, et al.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes initiating semaglutide (44,517 in Denmark, 16,860 in Norway) compared with initiators of SGLT2 inhibitors in national registries
funder: This study was funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (2025-00052B).
authorConflicts: Several authors participate in regulator-mandated phase IV studies funded by Novo Nordisk and other companies with funds to their institutions; one research group has received an unrestricted grant from Novo Nordisk; all stated as unrelated.
result: There were 32 NAION events among semaglutide users. Unadjusted incidence was 2.19 per 10,000 person-years on semaglutide against 1.18 on SGLT2 inhibitors in Denmark and 2.90 against 0.92 in Norway. Pooled adjusted hazard ratio 2.81 (95% CI 1.67 to 4.75); incidence rate difference +1.41 (0.53 to 2.29) per 10,000 person-years; per-protocol hazard ratio 6.35 (2.88 to 14.0). Self-controlled symmetry ratios were 1.14 (0.55 to 2.36) in Denmark and 2.67 (0.91 to 8.99) in Norway. Analyses for semaglutide in obesity were inconclusive.
